items.title: How many concurrent requests does a given traffic rate actually need?
items.description: Little's Law (L = λW): average concurrent requests equals the arrival rate times the average time each request spends in the system. Drag the request rate and average time-in-system — the defaults reproduce L2's own example (200 req/s, 150ms) landing at 30 concurrent requests.

items.title: How much does wait time actually change as utilization climbs?
items.description: The ρ/(1−ρ) queueing approximation from L3, shown relative to a 50% utilization baseline. Drag utilization from the near-miss case study's starting point (60%) toward its projected value (90%) and watch relative wait time move, not just utilization itself.
items.compute: const rho = params.utilization; const wait = rho / (1 - rho); const baseline = 0.5 / (1 - 0.5); return { relativeWait: wait / baseline };
